intervention_name: Digital Services Act
status_note: Regulation directly applies; major platform systemic-risk and recommender-transparency duties are operative.
coding_note: Codes the nonprofiled recommender option and recommender-system risk duties; minor protections are not treated as an account-access rule.

intervention_name: Online Safety Act 2023
status_note: Principal illegal-content and child-safety duties were operative by 2025-07-25.
coding_note: Codes platform risk duties where recommender systems must be assessed and mitigated; does not infer a categorical feed ban.

intervention_name: Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Act 2024
status_note: The account-restriction duty took effect on 2025-12-10.
coding_note: Codes the statutory reasonable-steps access restriction and age-assurance implementation, not broader safety-expectation duties.

intervention_name: Protecting Our Kids from Social Media Addiction Act
status_note: Addictive-feed restrictions and the private-account default remain operative; notification, annual-reporting, and like-count default requirements are enjoined.
coding_note: Coding separates operative feed restrictions from provisions affected by the injunction.
Core Intervention Summary: Bars covered services from giving minors personalized addictive feeds without verifiable parental consent, restricts notifications during specified overnight and school hours, and requires parent-set access and daily feed-time controls.

intervention_name: Social Media Safety Act
status_note: Permanently enjoined in federal district court; appeal pending at cutoff.
coding_note: Codes enacted access and parental-consent architecture even though currently blocked.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered social media companies to verify users’ ages and obtain verified parental consent before allowing minors to hold accounts, subject to the statute’s platform and service exclusions.

intervention_name: Utah Minor Protection in Social Media Act
status_note: Preliminary injunction blocks enforcement.
coding_note: Directly requires disablement of autoplay, continuous scrolling, and push notifications for minor accounts, plus supervisory daily time-limit and mandatory-break controls. Parental consent concerns alteration of default privacy settings rather than account access.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires social media services to disable autoplay, continuous scrolling, and engagement-prompting push notifications for minor accounts, and to offer activated supervisory tools for daily time limits and mandatory breaks.

intervention_name: Securing Children Online Through Parental Empowerment (SCOPE) Act
status_note: The monitoring-and-filtering requirement and related algorithm duty remain enjoined; age-registration and parental-control provisions remain operative after Fifth Circuit review.
coding_note: Age assurance is coded from the statutory duty to register age; recommender duty is limited to the express algorithm-related harm duty.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered services to register users’ ages before account creation, provide verified parents tools to supervise and limit minors’ use time, and make reasonable efforts concerning algorithms that recommend content to known minors.

intervention_name: Online Protections for Minors
status_note: The Eleventh Circuit stayed the preliminary injunction; provisions were enforceable at cutoff.
coding_note: Codes tiered account restriction, age assurance, and parental consent.
Core Intervention Summary: Prohibits covered social media platforms from maintaining accounts for children under 14 and requires verified parental consent for 14- and 15-year-olds, using age verification to apply the account restrictions.

intervention_name: Walker Montgomery Protecting Children Online Act
status_note: Emergency relief was denied and the law was enforceable while merits litigation continued.
coding_note: The safety-duty component is coded as a design-harm duty; no additional recommender restriction is inferred.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered social-interaction services to register and make reasonable efforts to verify account applicants’ ages, obtain parental consent for known minors’ accounts, and implement a strategy to mitigate specified harms to minors.

intervention_name: Parental Notification by Social Media Operators Act
official_name: Am. Sub. HB 33 (2023), Ohio Rev. Code § 1349.09
status_note: The appellate mandate was stayed, leaving the district-court injunction operative.
coding_note: Codes access and consent requirements notwithstanding the present block.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered social media operators to secure verifiable parental consent before a child under 16 agrees to service terms, with parental notice of account terms and privacy practices.

intervention_name: Protecting Children from Social Media Act
status_note: No injunction was operative at cutoff; preliminary-injunction proceedings were remanded.
coding_note: Codes account/access controls and parental time-control functionality.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered social media platforms to verify the ages of prospective account holders, obtain parental consent for minors to open accounts, and provide parental tools for supervision and limits on minors’ platform use.

intervention_name: Protecting Georgia's Children on Social Media Act of 2024
status_note: Social media provisions are preliminarily enjoined.
coding_note: Codes enacted access architecture only; school education provisions are outside scope.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered social media services to use age-verification methods for account holders and obtain parental consent before minors younger than 16 may maintain accounts.

intervention_name: Stop Addictive Feeds Exploitation (SAFE) for Kids Act
status_note: Final rules were published; statute and rules are scheduled for 2027-01-25.
coding_note: Codes default chronological/non-addictive feed protection and overnight notification restriction.
Core Intervention Summary: Prohibits covered platforms from providing addictive algorithmic feeds to minors without parental consent and restricts overnight notifications to minors, while preserving feeds based on user-selected or chronological content.

intervention_name: Social-media platform responsibilities and limits for minors
status_note: The statute took effect, then was preliminarily enjoined on 2026-02-27.
coding_note: Codes the minor time-use cap; age determination identifies users subject to the protection but is not coded as account/service Access.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires social media platforms to determine whether users are under 16 and limit those minors to one hour of use per day per service, subject to parent-authorized adjustments.

intervention_name: Secure Online Child Interaction and Age Limitation Act
status_note: Permanently enjoined as to affected NetChoice-member platforms; appeal pending at the cutoff.
coding_note: Codes the enacted access and supervisory time-use controls. The current statute gives the Division exclusive administration and enforcement authority.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered social media services to verify account applicants’ ages, obtain parental consent for minors’ accounts, and provide parents supervisory controls over minors’ daily use time and required breaks.

intervention_name: Protections for Youth Who Use Social Media
status_note: Section 4's youth-engagement information requirement, including the recurring-notification alternative, is preliminarily enjoined.
coding_note: Section 6-1-1601 permits compliance through either a broader youth engagement-information function or a recurring pop-up/full-screen notification pathway.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires qualifying social media platforms to give under-18 users information about their engagement, either through an information function or recurring pop-up warnings triggered by extended or late-night use.

intervention_name: Maryland Kids Code
status_note: Constitutional litigation remained pending; no injunction against enforcement had been entered as of the cutoff.
coding_note: The statute expressly disclaims required age gating and imposes a broader design and data-protection impact-assessment duty rather than a discrete recommender-system duty; design_harm_duty remains coded.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires online products reasonably likely to be accessed by children to assess child-related design and data risks, including engagement-extending features, and document steps aligning the product with children’s best interests.

intervention_name: Age-Appropriate Online Design Code Act
status_note: Current Nebraska statutes, as amended by LB 838 (2026), are operative from 2026-07-18.
coding_note: Codes chronological-feed choice and direct controls for covered design features, including autoplay, infinite scroll, notifications, and time limits. Age determination establishes applicability of child protections rather than conditioning account access.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered platforms to give minors controls over engagement features and a chronological-feed option, impose protective defaults, restrict certain notifications, and provide time-use controls under the statute amended in 2026.

intervention_name: Parental Rights in Social Media Act
status_note: Age-verification and parental-consent provisions are enjoined; other parental tools took effect.
coding_note: Coding records the enacted intervention while the status field captures the split operative posture.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered social media platforms to verify prospective account holders’ ages and secure parental consent for minors’ accounts, while offering parents tools to supervise accounts and limit use time.

intervention_name: Social Media Safety Act amendments
status_note: Preliminarily enjoined before delayed design provisions took effect.
coding_note: Separate intervention because the amendment added material design obligations.
Core Intervention Summary: Adds duties for covered platforms to avoid addiction-inducing practices involving recommendations and notifications, apply protective minor settings, restrict overnight notifications, audit compliance, and provide parental controls over access and use.

intervention_name: Social Media Platform Harm Liability Act
status_note: State enforcement is enjoined for affected NetChoice members; the order does not necessarily bar claims under the separate private cause of action.
coding_note: Codes an addictive-design restriction and generalized design-harm duty; it does not impose a discrete recommender-system duty.
Core Intervention Summary: Prohibits covered social media platforms from using a design, algorithm, or feature they know or reasonably should know causes specified harms, including addiction, and creates liability for violations.

intervention_name: Social Media Warning Law
status_note: Warning provisions become operative on 2027-01-01.
coding_note: Codes only the enacted warning/interruption requirement.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered social media platforms to display a warning to minors or users whose age is undetermined when accessing the service and after extended use, with specified duration and dismissal limits.

intervention_name: Covered Platform Age Restriction
status_note: Signed shortly before cutoff; scheduled effective date is 2027-01-01.
coding_note: Codes age restriction, age assurance, personalized-feed limits, addictive design, and autoplay from enacted text.
Core Intervention Summary: Bars covered platforms from giving users under 16 addictive feeds or autoplay, requires age checks before providing those features, and permits accounts for younger users only without the restricted features.

intervention_name: Social Media Mental Health Warning Label Law
status_note: The warning requirement took effect on 2026-07-01.
coding_note: Codes an access-session warning only; no recurring 30-minute timer appears in the enacted statute.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires a covered social media platform to present a mental-health warning when a user accesses the service, keeping it visible until the user acknowledges it or leaves.

intervention_name: Addictive Social Media Platform Warning Label Law
official_name: L.2025, c.689, as amended by L.2026, c.85; N.Y. GBL art. 45-A
age_threshold: Warning required unless user is reasonably determined to be over 17
status_note: Warning requirements are enacted but do not take effect until 2027-01-01.
coding_note: Codes required warning interruptions for covered young users under enacted GBL article 45-A. The underlying addictive features define scope but are not independently restricted by this intervention.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered platforms with addictive features to warn users not reasonably determined to be over 17 on initial and extended use, with repeat warnings at specified intervals; it does not ban those features.

intervention_name: Stop Harms from Addictive Social Media Act
status_note: Signed 2026-04-02 and effective 2026-07-01.
coding_note: Codes profile-based feed restrictions, autoplay, infinite scroll, gamified rewards, notifications, and parental time controls.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered platforms to obtain parental consent for children’s accounts, withhold profile-based feeds and specified addictive interface features from children, and offer parents controls over daily and scheduled use.

intervention_name: Age-Appropriate Code Design Act
status_note: Act 96 took effect upon approval on 2026-02-05.
coding_note: Codes minor-default nonprofiled choice plus named engagement-design restrictions and design-harm duty.
Core Intervention Summary: Requires covered platforms to exercise reasonable care against foreseeable harms to minors, provide user controls over recommendation and use settings, and apply protective defaults and limits to specified engagement features.

intervention_name: Vermont Age-Appropriate Design Code Act
status_note: The statute and required rules take effect on 2027-01-01.
coding_note: Codes personal-data recommendation limits, overnight notifications, and compulsive-use design regulation.
Core Intervention Summary: Restricts using minors’ personal data to recommend content absent a user request or setting, bars overnight push notifications to minors, and directs the regulator to adopt compulsive-use design rules.

intervention_name: Social Media Amendments — excessive-use liability
status_note: The statutory excessive-use liability framework has been effective since 2024-10-01.
coding_note: Codes liability tied to engagement-driven, algorithmically curated excessive use as recommender/design safety duties.
Core Intervention Summary: Creates a private liability framework for adverse mental-health outcomes allegedly caused by minors’ excessive use of algorithmically curated social media, with rebuttable presumptions tied to specified engagement-design practices.

intervention_name: Legal representative consent for minor online accounts
status_note: Act 16 is in force; it revised the minor-account framework before the earlier version took effect.
coding_note: Treated as the final enacted access intervention requiring legal-representative consent for a minor's online account contract.
Core Intervention Summary: Prohibits covered online services from making an account-creation contract with a minor without written consent from the minor’s legal representative, rendering nonconsensual contracts relatively null.

intervention_name: Digital Statute of the Child and Adolescent (ECA Digital)
official_name: Lei nº 15.211, de 17 de setembro de 2025
status_note: Lei nº 15.352/2026 established the statute's effective date as 2026-03-17.
coding_note: Codes age assurance, feed choice, addictive-design restriction, time-use controls, and design duties from the enacted statute.

intervention_name: Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendation in Internet Information Services
official_name: 国家互联网信息办公室等四部门令第9号
status_note: The regulation has been operative since 2022-03-01.
coding_note: Codes a non-personalized option, recommendation safety duties, and prohibition on addiction-inducing algorithms.

intervention_name: Regulations on the Protection of Minors in Cyberspace
status_note: The regulation has been operative since 2024-01-01.
coding_note: Codes anti-addiction duties, minor modes, time controls, and parental tools for covered online services.

intervention_name: Electronic System Governance for Child Protection (PP TUNAS)
age_threshold: Under 16 for high-risk account access; broader child duties under 18
status_note: PP 17/2025 is in force; the implementing regulation operationalized high-risk account restrictions from 2026-03-28.
coding_note: PP 17 and its 2026 implementing regulation are consolidated as one intervention; codes age-tiered access, assurance, consent, and child-protection duties.
